source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why can arithmetic on learned word vectors sometimes capture a relationship between concepts?

options.text: Relationships can be reflected in directions within the vector space.
options.feedback: A learned geometry can encode useful relationships. An analogy is an approximate pattern, not an exact identity guaranteed for every model.

options.text: Vocabulary identifiers are arranged as a ranked list of definitions.
options.feedback: Token identifiers identify vocabulary entries. Semantic geometry belongs to the learned vectors, not to a ranking of dictionary definitions.

options.text: Each vector contains a written rule for the requested word analogy.
options.feedback: Vectors are numerical representations rather than text instructions. Useful analogies can emerge from the learned arrangement.

options.text: Temperature performs concept arithmetic before embeddings are assigned.
options.feedback: Temperature affects output sampling later in the pipeline. It does not create the relationships in the embedding space.
